Born at Littlestown, Adams County, Pennsylvania, on 8 January 1798, son of Johann Adam Winterode and Maria Magdalena
Ashbaugh: Pennsylvania German farm country, a few miles from Gettysburg.
On 22 May 1836 he married Sarah Ann Weinbrenner at Saint Matthew’s Lutheran Church,
Hanover. He farmed in Mount Pleasant and then Cumberland Township, outside Gettysburg.
By 1860 he was on the Emmitsburg Road south of town, post office Green Mount: the census lists his neighbours as Jacob
Beamer and Alexander Currens, whose house and barn were burned in the battle three years later,
and the rise of the road there is still called Wintrode Ridge.
He is not on the county map of 1858, so he came there between 1858 and 1860.
1860 was his hardest year: Sarah Ann died in August, and in the last week of December a son of nineteen and his married
daughter Mary Ann Eckert died two days apart.
After the Confederate invasion he filed a border-damage claim for his losses.
His will of 1877 left five dollars to his son William Samuel and the rest of his estate equally to Edward Clinton
and his sisters Sarah Louise, Eliza Ann, Harriet Elizabeth, Maria Catherine and Laura Jane,
with one condition: should Laura Jane marry Peter Fraver, “the young man paying attention to her,”
her share was to go to the others. He died on 26 June 1877.
Born in Mount Pleasant Township, Adams County, Pennsylvania, in 1811, daughter of George Winebrenner of Hanover and
Sarah Patterson; her mother died when she was 13.
She married Samuel Wintrode at Saint Matthew’s Lutheran Church, Hanover, on 22 May 1836,
and raised a large family in Mount Pleasant and Cumberland townships.
She died in August 1860. In the last week of that December a son of nineteen and her married daughter,
Mary Ann Eckert, died two days apart.
